analysis: Examined the changes in ProviderLoop+ModelLoading.swift and ProviderLoop+ModelSelection.swift. Changed lines: in ModelLoading, unloadModel (head 1145-1149) makes selectedModelRecovery.makeAllDue after a Nemotron Super retirement, and again at 1216 after a normal unload. These only schedule a recheck of waiting selected models at the next capacity tick. They add no new input, trust boundary crossing, key handling, attestation change, or plaintext path. The lines around the weight-hash TOCTOU guard (head 552-666), hold refusal (577) and load-interruption checks (711, 945) are unchanged context. Unchanged context also holds the cached-hash/prefix-cache eligibility logic relevant to T-041, with cacheEligibleWeightHash set only when fresh cryptographic hashes are verified. In ModelSelection, the patch only snapshots and restores the new enabledModelsAtLastSwitch variable alongside hasPersistedModelSwitch. The rollback path restores it only when persistedReplacement was set, which matches the existing persistence rollback. I found no authorization, data-exposure or availability regression. Remaining integration questions: where enabledModelsAtLastSwitch is consumed (the declaration and consumers are not in the supplied evidence), and whether the extra makeAllDue calls in selectedModelRecovery could cause load storms. Both are unverified outside the supplied units. The effect appears limited to model-selection filtering and retry scheduling, and the unload makeAllDue calls only add bounded recheck work.
